title: Admin Skein: lightweight task-weaver for runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a compact 'skein' service that weaves existing runbook steps into verifiable, idempotent tasks that can be executed by support engineers or automated playflows. The skein should: 1) accept a runbook-as-task manifest (ordered steps with typed inputs), 2) execute steps in a sandboxed manner with explicit checkpoints and rollbacks, 3) emit structured telemetry for per-step timing/cost/side-effects, and 4) enforce RBAC and audit logging (KMS-backed request signatures). Goal is to reduce mean time to remediate for common incidents while preserving safety for sensitive environments (Dedicated/Private).
acceptance_criteria: Skein accepts a runbook manifest (YAML/JSON) and produces a task id
Each step runs in a sandbox (container or sidecar) and can be dry-runed without side-effects
System records per-step telemetry to the console telemetry pipeline (latency, tokens, external calls)
Replay and rollback primitives exist for at least 3 canonical runbooks (db-migration-fix, node-restart, cache-prune)
RBAC enforced: only roles with 'support:runbook:execute' can start non-dry runs; audit log entry is created for every non-dry action
End-to-end integration test passes in staging and a canary run is executed by oncall with documented run results
implementation_notes: We will implement a thin coordinator service in Go (existing operator patterns) that references the runlet DSL. Step runtime will be pluggable: default sandbox uses existing adminlet sidecar runner (less infra) and an experimental serverless executor for long-running maintenance steps. Telemetry hooks use the console ingestion (route: ops.playbook.steps). State checkpointing writes immutable snapshots to the runbook-store (S3) with hashed signatures to support safe replay. Avoid implementing a new DSL; reuse the runlet spec from ENG-314159 and extend with 'checkpoint' and 'safety-hints' fields.

risk_mitigation: To limit blast radius: default to dry-run mode for all users except those in the 'oncall:can-execute' group. Any non-dry runs require a two-person approval for Private deployments. Use feature flag 'skein:live-exec' scoped by org for gradual rollout. All non-dry runs create immutable audit blobs stored behind KMS and retained per compliance policy.
